statement: For a zero-dimensional osculating Grassmannian Schubert problem, the generic complex count is its Schubert intersection number, equivalently the specified tensor-product singular-weight-space dimension. Corollary 6.3 realizes exactly this many distinct real points at distinct real osculation parameters and proves transversality.

source.location: Corollary 6.3(ii), PDF p.28; Theorem 6.1 and Corollary 6.2, pp.26–27

notes:
The row retains arbitrary conjugation-invariant osculation data. Distinct real parameters supply a transverse witness and hence the generic complex count; no claim that every nonreal-parameter fibre is reduced is made. The weight λ includes the specified condition at infinity in the source notation.

Imported from the 2026-10-26 catalogue record R_3c8c14ea9e5616f8; the source claim has not been newly rechecked against the paper for this beta import.

The 2007 paper explicitly distinguishes the earlier Mukhin–Tarasov–Varchenko proof of reality from its new transversality theorem. Both are cited here; the intersection-number/representation-dimension equality itself is classical.
scope: Zero-dimensional Grassmannian Schubert problems restricted to flags osculating one rational normal curve; real lower bounds allow conjugate pairs, total reality/transversality requires distinct real osculation points.
